executive_summary: Across the three calls (Nov 2023, Dec 2024, Nov 2025), Saakshi Medtech shows a clear U-shaped trajectory: optimistic growth and diversification plans in FY24, a sharp operational and revenue setback in H1 FY25 due to customer-side deferrals, followed by a strong recovery and margin expansion in H1 FY26. Management credibility improves in the latest call, with earlier deferred themes (capacity consolidation, aerospace ramp-up) translating into measurable delivery. Key themes include high customer concentration risk, gradual diversification into aerospace, EV and data-center linked fabrication, and a decisive shift toward higher-margin, value-added segments. Execution risk remains, but FY26 commentary shows better specificity and confidence backed by numbers.

evidence.statement: ‘We are still comfortable in terms of getting a revenue growth of around 20% for the next couple of years… probably in the next quarter call, maybe we’ll be giving you a very encouraging number.’ – optimistic but aspirational.

‘This was primarily due to market-specific demand fluctuations, temporary stop in operations for few of our bigger customers… orders have not been cancelled, but deferred.’ – more defensive, explanatory tone.
‘H1 FY26 marks the start of this… a significant 31% revenue surge year-on-year… EBITDA has improved to 18.71%.’ – confident tone backed by delivery.
‘We’ve clocked over Rs.1 crore from aerospace in H1 FY26 versus Rs.0.14 crore last year… nearly a seven-fold increase.’ – specific, data-backed articulation.

guidance_vs_delivery.what_was_delivered: H1FY26 revenue up 31% YoY; EBITDA margin expanded to 18.7%.

guidance_evolution.pattern_summary: Management initially set aspirational targets, revised them downward during FY25 stress, and regained credibility in FY26 by delivering on deferred capacity and diversification initiatives.

margin_commentary: Margins were initially guided as ‘maintainable’ in FY24. H1FY25 saw margin pressure due to operating deleverage and revenue decline, though cost control was emphasized. In H1FY26, EBITDA expanded sharply to ~18.7%, driven by operating leverage, higher contribution from aerospace and engineered assemblies, and facility consolidation. Margin guidance now sounds more credible, with management explicitly stating sustainability rather than aggressive expansion.
revenue_growth_narrative: The growth story evolved from steady OEM-led expansion (renewables, panels) to a disruption-led pause in FY25 due to customer deferrals (GE Vernova, textile OEM). Subsequently, growth drivers shifted toward aerospace, EV panels (Mahindra), and data-center linked fabrication (radiators). The narrative has shifted from broad optimism to segment-specific, execution-backed growth.
key_risks_flagged_by_management: High dependence on a few large OEM customers; order deferrals directly impact revenue (Q2FY24, H1FY25).
Regulatory changes in medical devices slowing scale-up (Q2FY24, H1FY25).
Long qualification and certification cycles in aerospace delaying revenue realization (H1FY25, H1FY26).
Project-based businesses (data centers, defense) have long tendering and RFQ cycles (H1FY25).
positive_signals: First Saakshi-branded X-ray system received AERB, BIS, CDSCO approvals; revenue expected from Q4FY24 (Q2FY24).
Export share increased from ~2.5% FY23 to over 5% by FY25 (H1FY25).
Aerospace revenue grew ~7x YoY in H1FY26 (H1FY26).
EBITDA margin expansion to ~18.7% in H1FY26 (H1FY26).
₹250 Cr, 5-year EV panel order from Mahindra with ~₹230 Cr yet to be executed (H1FY26).
red_flags: Repeated deferral of large customer orders (GE Vernova, textile OEM) across multiple quarters without firm restart dates (H1FY25).
Very high customer concentration acknowledged (top 5 = ~90–95% revenue) with slow diversification (Q2FY24).
Limited long-term order book visibility (only 3-month visibility cited repeatedly) – ‘we don’t have a one-year order book’ (H1FY26).

business_problems_and_challenges.problem: High dependency on a few large OEM customers leads to revenue volatility when their operations are delayed.
business_problems_and_challenges.evidence: ‘Temporary stop in operations for few of our bigger customers… orders have been deferred’ (H1FY25).

business_problems_and_challenges.problem: Long and complex certification and qualification cycles in aerospace and medical devices delay monetization.
business_problems_and_challenges.evidence: ‘Qualification times for aviation business would be almost close to a year’ (H1FY26); ‘medical business plagued with regulatory developments’ (H1FY25).

business_problems_and_challenges.problem: Lack of integrated data visibility and long-term order forecasting; only short-term (quarterly) visibility available.
business_problems_and_challenges.evidence: ‘We typically have only a 3-month visibility in terms of order book’ (H1FY26).

overall_investment_signal: cautious_positive: Execution credibility has improved sharply in FY26 with revenue and margin delivery, but high customer concentration and limited order-book visibility warrant caution despite strong optionality in aerospace and EV segments.
